bear.narrative: A genuine down cycle, not a slower recovery. The replacement calender suffers a commissioning failure in the fourth quarter, so FY2026E revenue lands below the nine-month run-rate, and the import flood does not ease: revenue grows 8pp less a year than the base, which produces falling revenue in FY2029E and FY2030E. Dumped plastic keeps domestic utilisation near the 60-70% the association reports, the trade remedies INAPLAS asked for at the November 2026 meeting with the industry ministry are not imposed, resin costs stay near the deck's FY2026E Brent of 96.0 and the 15% unpassed exposure bites harder, taking the at-cost gross margin down 5.5pp so the reported FY2026E margin falls below the FY2025 11.8% trough. Working capital absorbs more cash. The controller loan is called and has to be refinanced on the bank lines at a distress spread, which is the 1pp addition to the cost of capital; the free-float placement is done at a discount rather than at the market price [S2, S4, S5, F12, F21].

bull.narrative: The calender runs from the fourth quarter of 2026 at nameplate, the industry ministry imposes an anti-dumping or safeguard measure, and domestic utilisation moves from the 60-70% the association reports toward the 80-90% it says is possible, so revenue grows 5.6pp a year faster than the base and reaches about 82% of the 29,600 MT productive base by FY2030E, which is 69% of the 35,000 MT nameplate. The fixed factory overhead of IDR59.8bn spreads across those tonnes, lifting the at-cost gross margin 5.5pp; the reported margin reaches, but does not exceed, the FY2023 peak of 24.9% by FY2030E. Resin costs fall faster than the deck's Brent path as the FY2027E-2028E supply build lands, working capital turns quicker, the PP and HIPS line finally earns its capital, and the refinancing risk on the controller loan recedes, which is the 1pp reduction in the cost of capital [S2, S4, S5, F11, F26].

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +15.8% to IDR347.9bn. This is no longer a forecast from the first half: nine-month 2026 revenue was IDR247.30bn, so the fourth quarter has to deliver IDR100.65bn, 15% above the third quarter's IDR87.58bn, for the year to land here [S7]. That is what a calender that only restarts after mid-2026 makes possible, and it is still 33% below the company's own IDR520.94bn target, a target it missed by 21% in 2025 [S2, F17, F19, F23]. FY2027E +15.5% to IDR401.9bn is the first full year of the replacement calender and takes revenue just past the FY2024 peak of IDR399.7bn [S0]. FY2028E +11.0%, FY2029E +8.5% and FY2030E +7.0% fill capacity that is already installed rather than new capital, and taper toward the 3.0% long run, which is the house terminal-growth cap rather than a deck series. Implied utilisation, at the FY2025 revenue per tonne of IDR27.39m and on the 29,600 MT productive base, is 42.9% in FY2026E, 49.6% in FY2027E, 55.0% in FY2028E, 59.7% in FY2029E and 63.9% in FY2030E; on the full 35,000 MT nameplate those are 36.3%, 41.9%, 46.5%, 50.5% and 54.0% [S2, F5, F6, F26]. The FY2030E figure is inside the 60-70% band the industry association reports for domestic plants today, which is the test the previous version of this model failed [S4, S5].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: 20.2% at FY2025A input costs, flat. This is a margin-at-normal-utilisation judgement, not a forecast of the reported margin, and the bridge from the last undisrupted year is explicit. FY2024 earned 17.2% at roughly 14,600 MT, about 49% of the 29,600 MT productive base [S2, S0]. Factory overhead was IDR59.76bn in FY2025, or IDR5.45m per tonne at 10,970 MT and about IDR4.09m per tonne at FY2024 volume; at the 18,900 MT implied by FY2030E revenue it falls to about IDR3.16m per tonne, which on revenue per tonne of IDR27.39m is worth about 3.4pp of gross margin [S2, F5, F11]. Adding that absorption to FY2024's 17.2% gives about 20.6%; we hold 20.2% to allow for the PP and HIPS line, which the company concedes has not delivered the returns expected of it, and for a mix that is less favourable than FY2024's [S2, F26]. The ten-year reported range in the annual report's financial highlights is 17.6, 14.4, 13.4, 17.7, 14.5, 15.0, 20.7, 24.9, 17.2 and 11.8 per cent, so 20.2% at normal volume sits between the average and the FY2023 peak rather than at the peak [S2]. The FY2026E-FY2030E reported margin is then 16.8%, 18.2%, 18.7%, 19.0% and 19.4% once the Brent link is applied, because the deck's Brent is 41% above the FY2025 average in FY2026E and only 10% above it by FY2030E [S0]. The nine-month 2026 actual margin of 16.55% and the third-quarter 17.3% are the anchor for the FY2026E figure [S7]. We deliberately do not carry the 24.9% of FY2023: that year had a 41% lower resin cost and no import flood, and the associations now put industry utilisation at 60-70% because of dumped imports [S4, S5].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: 0.70, the raw-material share of cost of goods sold: IDR186.03bn of raw materials against IDR264.89bn of COGS in FY2025, with factory overhead at IDR59.76bn (22.6%), direct labour at IDR19.09bn and packing at IDR3.52bn [S2, F10, F11]. The resins are petrochemical - polypropylene, polyethylene and PET sheet - so Brent prices the feedstock; the company itself attributes the FY2025 margin compression partly to raw-material and energy prices [S2]. We do not use 1.0 because roughly 30% of COGS is rupiah overhead, wages and packaging that do not move with oil.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: 0.85, and this is an explicit judgment, not a sourced fact. The annual report contains no pricing-policy statement: searches for harga jual, menyesuaikan harga and kenaikan harga return no passage in which the company says it sets prices to cover costs, so the previous version's citation of S2 for that proposition was wrong and is withdrawn. The number is a judgment about a made-to-order industrial converter with no customer above 10% of revenue, which gives it more room to reprice than a branded consumer business but less than a producer with a tight market [S2, F25]. It is not 1.0 because the industry association says domestic plants run at only 60-70% of capacity because imported plastic is being sold at dumping prices, which caps how much of a cost rise can be pushed into price [S4, S5]. The value sensitivity is direct: at 100% pass-through the FY2026E reported gross margin is about 3.4pp higher than at 85%, taking it to the 20.2% at-cost level, and at 70% it is about 3.4pp lower, about 13.3%, because the retained exposure is 0.70 x (1 - pass-through) of COGS applied to a Brent move of 41% [S0]. The 70% case does not return to the FY2025 trough of 11.8% because volumes have recovered by then; it is the margin the plant earns if it recovers none of the resin increase. We use 85% because the nine-month 2026 gross margin of 16.55% was earned with Brent averaging well above the FY2025 level, which is evidence that most of the cost move was recovered in price [S7].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 12.8% on IDR347.9bn, i.e. about IDR44.5bn of selling and general-and-administrative cost, up from IDR41.84bn in FY2025 because selling cost scales with the recovered volume [S2]. Nine-month 2026 selling and administrative cost was IDR32.65bn on revenue of IDR247.30bn, 13.2%, so the full-year ratio requires the fourth quarter to run at about 11.8%, which is what the third quarter's 12.7% and the shrinking electronics business support [S7, S2, F9]. The ratio then falls to 11.9%, 11.2%, 10.8% and 10.5% as revenue grows against a largely fixed cost base: the FY2025 ratio was 13.9% only because revenue collapsed 24.8% under a fixed establishment, and the FY2023 ratio on IDR469.1bn of sales was 10.7% [S2, F20]. The electronics business, which lost IDR2.29bn at the operating line in FY2025 on IDR7.43bn of sales, is being scaled down and its cost is the first to go [S2, F9]. We stop at 10.5% rather than the FY2023 10.7% because the new calender adds depreciation and technical staff rather than removing them.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A was IDR29.16bn against revenue of IDR300.47bn, 9.7%, once the fixed-asset note is used instead of the data pack's selling-and-G&A share of 5.98 [S2, F1, F2]. The ratio falls to 9.2% in FY2026E and 7.7% by FY2030E because the denominator grows while the charge grows only with the IDR40bn of 2026 capital spending; the absolute charge rises from IDR32.0bn to IDR40.0bn.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 14.6% or IDR50.7bn, rebased on the nine-month filing. Capital expenditures booked in the nine months to 30 September 2026 were IDR42.553bn [S7, F39], of which IDR36.798bn is the replacement calender standing in assets under construction at that date [S7, F40]; cash advances for fixed assets were IDR46.655bn and the advance balance rose from IDR8.250bn to IDR12.352bn, so the cash outlay is IDR4.10bn above the additions booked [S7, F41, F42]. We add about IDR4.0bn for the fourth quarter - completion of the calender plus routine maintenance - to the IDR46.7bn cash outlay, giving IDR50.7bn. FY2025 capex was IDR36.52bn against D&A of IDR29.16bn [S2, F1, S0]. From FY2027E we hold capex at 7.7% falling to 6.4%, roughly equal to D&A, because the machine is installed and what remains is maintenance plus the PP sheet line, which the annual report says did not deliver the returns expected of it [S2]. We do not carry a second expansion: the productive base is 29,600 MT against 10,970 MT produced, so the next rupiah of growth comes from filling the plant, not building another.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: 21% in FY2026E, 19% thereafter. The FY2025 ratio was 20.8% on the data pack's working-capital line against revenue, but the June 2026 balance sheet shows inventory and receivables rebuilt ahead of the machine restart, which is why we start above the FY2024 ratio of 16.7% and let it normalise as the stock converts to sales [S0, S2]. The FY2025 inventory build and the IDR2.36bn rise in taxes payable are in the same filing [S2].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 22%, the Indonesian corporate rate. The FY2025 effective rate was 19.4% (tax IDR1.35bn on pre-tax profit IDR6.98bn) and FY2024 was 25.5%, so the statutory rate is the neutral assumption rather than either year's accident [S2]. The nine-month 2026 effective rate was 37.0% (tax IDR4.39bn on pre-tax profit IDR11.84bn), which we treat as a timing or non-deductible item rather than a new run rate, because it is far above both the statutory rate and the two prior years [S7].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 7.44%, FY2025 finance costs of IDR1.668bn over opening debt of IDR22.424bn of short-term bank loans [S2, F3]. This rate is used for interest expense on the bank lines in the profit and loss, NOT for the WACC: the engine builds the pre-tax cost of debt in the cost of capital as the rupiah risk-free rate plus the deck's corporate debt spread, which is 9.45%, and the 7.44% input does not enter that calculation. The distinction is stated in the report so the prose matches the model. The rate is applied to bank borrowings only: the IDR41.15bn controller loan that sits in the same note is non-interest-bearing, so including it in the base would understate the true cost of the bank lines [S2, F12, F13].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 2.87%, FY2025 finance income of IDR3.600bn over opening cash and equivalents [S2, S0]. The yield falls as the IDR60bn dividend paid on 26 June 2026 shrinks the cash base [S3, F21].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero. The company repaid IDR1.39bn of short-term bank loans in FY2025 and has net cash; the dividend is funded from the balance sheet, not from new debt [S2, S3]. The 30 September 2026 balance sheet confirms it: bank loans fell a further IDR0.87bn to IDR26.03bn while cash rose to IDR41.23bn [S7].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero from FY2026E. FY2025 carried IDR11.91bn of other income of which IDR8.74bn was the fire insurance claim and IDR0.22bn a gain on asset sales, plus IDR0.61bn of other expense; none of it repeats [S2, F15, F16]. The nine-month 2026 accounts carry IDR3.93bn of other income, of which IDR0.63bn is a gain on asset sales and IDR3.30bn is an unexplained lain-lain line, and IDR0.40bn of other expense; we exclude all of it from the forecast because the nature of the lain-lain item is not disclosed and it is not an operating cash flow [S7]. Excluding the FY2025 items, the FY2025 operating result was a loss of IDR6.2bn, which is the trough the forecast recovers from.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Zero: the minority interest in the consolidated subsidiary is immaterial in both FY2025 and FY2024 [S2].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: 25% from FY2026E, which is deliberately NOT the FY2025 payout. The Rp44.03 a share approved on 25 May 2026 covers FY2025 and the previous financial year in one payment, cost about IDR60bn and was 10.7 times FY2025 net profit; it is a catch-up distribution out of retained earnings, not a policy rate, and it is already paid (26 June 2026) before the valuation balance sheet [S3, F21]. The engine pays last year's declared DPS, so the FY2026E cash flow carries the IDR60bn correctly. After it, cash fell from IDR116.0bn at end-2025 to IDR31.2bn at 30 June 2026 and has since rebuilt to IDR41.2bn at 30 September 2026, and the group is in net debt once the controller loan is counted, so the next dividend has to be funded from earnings [S0, S2, S7, F12]. The dividend policy in the annual report is discretionary, decided at each AGM, with no ratio [S2]; the record is a skipped dividend for FY2022, IDR7.49bn for FY2023 and this catch-up, so we assume a modest 25% rather than a return to the Rp44.03 level.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero in the forecast, with the free-float placement quantified rather than modelled. 1,362,671,400 shares are issued and paid up and no rights issue is announced [S2, S0]. The data pack's free float is 7.81% against the exchange's 15% minimum for holders below 5%, a gap of 7.19pp with a 31 March 2029 deadline; closing it by placing new shares at the current price would need about 115.3m new shares, an 8.5% increase, raising about IDR29.75bn at IDR258 [S0, S2]. That is close to value-neutral per share: the cash raised at the market price is worth approximately what the new shares dilute, so a placement at the current price does not reduce the DCF value per share and is not put through the share count, which the engine applies to the profit-and-loss lines but not to the DCF denominator. A discounted placement is a real cost and is carried in the bear narrative, where a 20% discount would cost about 1.5% of intrinsic value per share. The annual report itself links the free-float rule to the buyback: it says a buyback is constrained by the rule that at least 15% must be held by the public below 5%, which is why the unused buyback authorization was not used [S2].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 3.0%, the house terminal-growth cap for a rupiah name: a rounded midpoint of the deck's rupiah long-run inflation anchor and its CPI assumption, below the template's IDR terminal cap and below the 5.29% real GDP growth the deck carries for Indonesia, because a converter with 70% of COGS in a globally traded feedstock grows with volume and resin prices, not with nominal GDP [S0]. It is not itself a deck series, and the report describes it as a house cap rather than as the deck's inflation rate.

challenges.challenge: The target gives 40% weight to two multiples the report itself says are the wrong method for this name. Line 98 states that a cyclical converter at a trough cannot be valued on a trailing earnings multiple; line 108 says the multiple legs are kept as a floor but 'we do not let them drive the target'. In the model they are 25% EV/EBITDA and 15% P/E, and because they are struck on trough LTM EBITDA of 10.33bn and LTM net profit of 14.58bn they value the shares at 12.83 and 86.25 against the DCF's 184.13. The blend is 126.62, so the multiple legs account for 57.5 of the 57.5-point gap from the DCF to the blended value (45% of v0), even though their configured weight is 40%. The published target of 123.24 is therefore a trough-multiple target with a DCF overlay, not a DCF target, and the prose misdescribes it. VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL calls valuing a cyclical on current-year multiples the procyclical error #1 and requires through-cycle NAV at a sourced through-cycle price as the primary output.
challenges.answer: The challenge is right and it is the reason the target was wrong. The weights are now dcf_fcff 1.0, ev_ebitda 0.0 and pe 0.0, so the published target is a DCF target. The multiple legs are retained only as a floor exhibit: what the shares would be worth if the trough were the new normal. The engine's multiple legs are hard-wired to trailing LTM figures and cannot be re-based on normalised earnings without editing the engine, which the role forbids, so removing their weight is the honest fix. The sentence that the multiples do not drive the target is now true, and the report says the DCF is the target.

challenges.challenge: The conclusion that the price implies 'a return to peak-cycle profitability' (line 116) and that the market is 'capitalising a better operating outcome than any cell we are prepared to defend' (line 112) is contradicted by the report's own bull case. The bull is assigned 25% probability and its target is 294.09, 14% above the 258 price; its gross margin is 22.0% at base input costs, below the FY2023 24.9% the report calls peak. The sensitivity grid's top cell is 217.63 only because the grid varies growth and gross margin and holds the bull's working-capital and capex relief constant; the bull adds those two shocks and reaches 294.09. Either the bull is defensible, in which case the price is not above every defensible outcome and does not require peak-cycle margins, or it is not, in which case its 25% weight overstates the target. The report cannot have it both ways.
challenges.answer: The bull is defensible and the price is not beyond every defensible outcome, so the thesis is restated rather than the bull cut. The sensitivity grid varies only revenue growth and gross margin; the bull also carries the working-capital release and the lower cost of capital, which is why it sits above the grid's top cell. The report now says the price sits between the base and the bull, not beyond both, and the summary no longer claims the market capitalises an outcome no cell defends. The bull's reported margin reaches, but does not exceed, the FY2023 peak of 24.9 per cent, so it is a remedy scenario rather than a peak-cycle assumption.

challenges.challenge: The base case ignores the company's own 2026 operating-profit target and the second-quarter run-rate. F18, in fund record but never cited in the report, is a 2026 operating-profit target of 34.68bn on a 520.94bn sales target, a 6.7% operating margin. The model's FY2026E EBIT is 11.26bn, a 3.2% margin, less than a third of the target; even applying the 2025 realisation of 78.79% to F18 gives 27.32bn, 2.4 times the model. The second quarter of 2026 already earned 6.42bn of EBIT on 86.77bn of sales, a 7.4% margin, and 17.15bn of gross profit, a 19.8% gross margin; the model's full-year gross margin is 16.0%, which implies a second-half gross margin of about 15.95%, below the second-quarter exit rate even as the replacement calender restarts. The report uses F17 (the sales target) but not F18 (the operating-profit target), and it does not reconcile FY2026E to the Q2 run-rate.
challenges.answer: FY2026E is now anchored on the nine-month accounts, not on a first-half extrapolation. Nine-month revenue was IDR247.30bn and gross profit IDR40.93bn, a 16.55 per cent margin, so the fourth quarter has to deliver IDR100.65bn for our IDR347.9bn year. The reported FY2026E gross margin is 16.8 per cent, essentially the nine-month actual, and the fourth quarter holds the third quarter's 17.3 per cent. Clean operating profit for nine months was IDR8.29bn after stripping IDR3.93bn of other income and IDR0.40bn of other expense; we forecast IDR13.8bn for the year, which requires a fourth quarter at a 5.5 per cent clean operating margin against the third quarter's 4.6 per cent, on revenue a little above the third quarter's. F18's IDR34.68bn target is not attainable: nine months delivered IDR8.29bn clean and the fourth quarter would have to earn IDR26.4bn, and the company realised only 78.79 per cent of its 2025 sales target.

challenges.challenge: The base case assumes Asiaplast's utilisation stays far below the industry's for the whole forecast. At the FY2025 revenue per tonne of 27.39m IDR/MT, FY2027E revenue of 390.05bn implies 14,241 MT, 40.7% of the 35,000 MT capacity; FY2030E revenue of 469.75bn implies 17,151 MT, 49.0%. The industry association says domestic plants already run at 60-70% and could reach 80-90% if imports are curbed [S4, S5]. Even the bull case, at +3.5pp growth a year, implies only about 20,100 MT, 57% of capacity, in FY2030E - still below the industry's current 60-70%. The report treats the remedy as the 'single largest potential positive' (line 136) but the bull does not model the utilisation recovery it would produce, and never explains why Asiaplast permanently runs 10-20pp below the industry.
challenges.answer: The volume path is raised and the implied utilisation is now stated by year. The productive base is 29,600 MT, not 35,000 MT, because 5,400 MT of PP and HIPS capacity was added in 2025 and the company says the new machines are still very lightly used. On that base the forecast implies 42.9 per cent in FY2026E, 49.6 per cent in FY2027E, 55.0 per cent in FY2028E, 59.7 per cent in FY2029E and 63.9 per cent in FY2030E, so the base case reaches the industry's current 60-70 per cent band by the end of the explicit forecast. On the full nameplate the FY2030E figure is 54.0 per cent. The bull reaches about 78 per cent of the productive base, just below the 80-90 per cent band the association says a remedy would allow.

challenges.challenge: The bear is a slower recovery, not a down cycle, and its stated risks are not in the model. Bear revenue growth is base minus 3.5pp, so FY2026E is still +12.3% and FY2027E +8.6%: there is no down year anywhere in a scenario whose narrative says the import flood does not ease and the recovery arrives a year late. Bear gross margin is 17.0% at base input costs (about 13.5% reported in FY2026E), above the FY2025 actual 11.8% trough. The bear narrative says 'the controller loan is called for cash that the group no longer has', but the four shocks are only revenue growth, gross margin, working capital and capex; net borrowing is zero in every scenario, so the loan call and any refinancing cost are absent from the numbers. The free-float dilution is also absent (see C12).
challenges.answer: The bear is now a down cycle. Revenue growth is 8pp a year below the base, which produces falling revenue in FY2029E and FY2030E; the at-cost gross margin falls 5.5pp to 14.7 per cent, so the reported FY2026E margin of about 11.3 per cent is below the FY2025 trough of 11.8 per cent; working capital absorbs more cash; and the cost of capital rises 1pp because the controller loan is called and refinanced on the bank lines at a distress spread. The narrative now matches the shocks: the loan call is the WACC addition, and the free-float placement is done at a discount rather than at the market price.

challenges.challenge: The QC calibration gap is 4.80pp of EBITDA margin (FY2025A actual 7.63% against the model's 12.44%) and is not justified in qc_justifications, which cover only drift.capex_pct and extreme_call. The report explains the recovery in prose but does not bridge the 4.80pp. Separately, the extreme_call justification says the business earns '4.9% on equity'; no year in the model matches that: FY2025A ROE is 1.62%, FY2026E 3.12%, FY2027E 5.51% and FY2030E 8.26%. The 4.9% is unsourced and appears stale.
challenges.answer: The calibration gap is now justified in qc_justifications and bridged in the report. FY2025A EBITDA margin was 7.63 per cent; FY2026E is 13.2 per cent, a 5.5pp gap. The bridge is gross margin +5.0pp from overhead absorption and the Brent-linked reported margin, SG&A ratio +1.1pp as the fixed establishment spreads over a larger revenue base, and D&A ratio -0.5pp. The nine-month actual revenue and gross margin anchor the bridge, so it is evidence rather than a forecast. The stale 4.9 per cent ROE is corrected to the FY2030E model year, 9.5 per cent. The extreme_call justification, whose grid claim is no longer true, is removed rather than rewritten: the flag no longer fires because the target is at the price.

challenges.challenge: The 85% pass-through is one of the three value drivers and it is presented as sourced when it is not. The link1_pass basis says 'the company states that it sets selling prices to cover its costs' [S2], but the archived annual report contains no such statement: greps for 'harga jual', 'menyesuaikan harga' and 'kenaikan harga' return no pricing-policy passage. The number is not calibrated to the FY2022-FY2025 margin history either, and the report's own risk section says 70% would make the FY2026E margin 'materially worse' without quantifying it. The 19.5% at-cost gross margin is also 2.8pp above the ten-year average of 16.7% in the assumptions' own record and 2.3pp above FY2024's 17.2%, with no bridge from FY2024 at FY2025A resin costs to 19.5%.
challenges.answer: The 85 per cent pass-through is relabelled an explicit judgment and the false S2 citation is withdrawn: the annual report contains no pricing-policy statement. The number is now supported by the nine-month evidence, because a 16.55 per cent gross margin was earned with Brent well above the FY2025 average, which shows most of the cost move was recovered. The value sensitivity is stated: 100 per cent pass-through adds about 3.4pp to the FY2026E reported margin, taking it to the 20.2 per cent at-cost level, and 70 per cent subtracts about the same, taking it to about 13.3 per cent. The 3.4pp gap between the at-cost and the reported margin is exactly the 15 per cent of the linked cost that is not passed at 85 per cent. The 20.2 per cent at-cost gross margin is bridged from FY2024's 17.2 per cent: at FY2024's roughly 49 per cent utilisation factory overhead was about IDR4.09m a tonne, and at the 18,900 MT implied by FY2030E it falls to about IDR3.16m, worth about 3.4pp of margin, which takes 17.2 to about 20.6; we hold 20.2 to allow for the underperforming PP and HIPS line and mix. The 13.3 per cent case is not the FY2025 trough, because volumes have recovered; it is the margin the plant earns if it recovers none of the resin increase.

challenges.challenge: The report says revenue 'does not exceed the FY2022 peak at any point in the forecast' (line 80). In the model's own forecast it does: FY2022A revenue is 526.83bn, FY2034E is 528.71bn and FY2035E is 544.57bn. The claim is used to argue the forecast assumes recovery, not expansion; the visible table stops at FY2030E (469.75bn), which is why the error is easy to miss, but the DCF runs to FY2035E.
challenges.answer: The sentence is corrected. The explicit five-year forecast, FY2026E to FY2030E, does not exceed the FY2022 peak of IDR526.83bn: FY2030E is IDR517.88bn. The model crosses the peak in FY2031E at IDR533.42bn and reaches IDR600.37bn in FY2035E. The report now says through FY2030E and states the crossing year.

challenges.challenge: The cost-of-capital prose does not describe the model. Line 100 says the cost of debt is 'the rate the FY2025 accounts imply' (assumptions cost_of_debt 7.44%, from F3 finance costs over opening bank debt), but the model's kd_pre_tax is 9.45%, which is rf 7.45% plus a 2.00% corporate debt spread; the 7.44% input is not used in the WACC. Line 100 also calls the 7.65% D/E the company's 'net debt to equity', but 7.65% is gross bank debt of 26.897bn over market cap of 351.569bn; net debt is negative 4.27bn (net cash) on bank lines and positive 36.88bn only if the controller loan is included. The beta is re-levered at 7.65%, a definition that matches neither the net-cash nor the including-loan balance sheet.
challenges.answer: The prose now describes the model. The pre-tax cost of debt in the WACC is the rupiah risk-free rate of 7.45 per cent plus the deck's 2.00 per cent corporate spread, 9.45 per cent. The 7.44 per cent cost_of_debt input is used for interest expense on the bank lines in the profit and loss, not in the WACC, and the assumptions say so. The D/E of 7.65 per cent is gross bank debt over market capitalisation, which is the definition the engine uses to re-lever beta; the report says that explicitly and does not call it net debt to equity. Net debt is negative on bank lines and positive only when the controller loan is included, and that is the figure used for the net-debt/trough-EBITDA ratio.

challenges.challenge: The P/E leg does not carry the controller-loan bridge, contrary to the written claim. The assumptions' post_bs_review says 'the DCF, the EV/EBITDA and the P/E legs all carry the same burden', but the engine applies the bridge only to EV/EBITDA and EV/sales: for P/E it computes equity value as multiple times LTM net profit with no subtraction (m_multiple, calculation engine lines 920-922). The P/E leg's stored bridge of 36.75bn is reported but not applied, so its 86.25/share is overstated by 36.75/1,362.67 = 27.0/share; at the 15% weight that is about 4.05/share on v0 and about 5/share on the target. The direction is conservative (the published target is too high), but the method and the prose disagree.
challenges.answer: The P/E leg now carries zero weight, so its failure to subtract the controller loan cannot move the target. The engine computes the P/E leg as multiple times net profit with no bridge, which is engine behaviour we cannot change without editing the engine. The report labels the multiple legs as a floor exhibit and states that the P/E floor is flattered by about IDR30 a share because it does not carry the loan. The sentence claiming all three legs carry the same burden is removed from post_bs_review.

challenges.challenge: The report cites the commodity-cyclical card but does not deliver its output contract. There is no sourced through-cycle resin or product price and no NAV/share at a through-cycle price versus NAV at spot; no cost-curve quartile or cash-cost position; no dividend-capacity yield versus the NAV anchor (the report discusses the dividend but not its capacity yield); and no net-debt/trough-EBITDA. The scenario probabilities also sit away from the base rate: data/base_rates.yaml gives commodity_capex_turnaround a 42% hit rate with a +75% up move over three years on 40 observations, while the report assigns the bull 25% and never cites the base rate. The card's central rule - never value a cyclical on spot or current-year multiples - is the rule C1 shows the target breaks.
challenges.answer: The commodity-cyclical output contract is now delivered in section 4. Through-cycle Brent is the deck's long-run USD75 a barrel against a spot of USD97.1, reached in steps from the deck's USD96.0 in FY2026E and USD78.0 in FY2029E, so the DCF is a through-cycle NAV rather than a spot-price NAV; the report states the NAV at the through-cycle price and notes that holding Brent at spot would raise near-term cash flow but not the terminal value. The cost-curve position is given as the trough-year EBITDA margin and overhead per tonne, because a converter has no published cash-cost quartile. Dividend-capacity yield is shown against the intrinsic value, and net debt over trough EBITDA is shown including the controller loan. The 25 per cent bull is reconciled to the 42 per cent base rate: the base rate covers commodity producers' capex turnarounds, while this bull requires a specific policy decision that has not been announced, so it is weighted below the base rate rather than at it.

challenges.challenge: The free-float requirement is described but not quantified, and the dilution is not in the model. The data pack's free float is 7.81% against the exchange's 15% minimum (S2 p.20 states the 15% rule for public holders below 5%); the model's konglo block records a 7.19pp gap and a 2029-03-31 deadline. To close the gap by placing new shares to the public, the company would need about 115m new shares (an 8.5% increase on 1,362.67m), assuming the placement is the only route and is done at the current price; a discounted placement or a rights issue would be larger. The model's share_change is 0.0 in every year and scenario, so none of this dilution is valued, and the report's only treatment is that the discount rate 'affects' the minority stake (line 148).
challenges.answer: The dilution is quantified. The data pack's free float is 7.81 per cent against the 15 per cent minimum, a 7.19pp gap; closing it by placing new shares at the current price needs about 115.3m new shares, an 8.5 per cent increase, raising about IDR29.75bn. The forecast share count is unchanged because a placement at the market price is close to value-neutral per share: the cash raised is worth approximately what the new shares dilute, and the engine applies share_change to the profit-and-loss lines but not to the DCF denominator, so putting the shares through without the cash would overstate the dilution. A discounted placement is a real cost and is carried in the bear narrative, where a 20 per cent discount costs about 1.5 per cent of intrinsic value per share. The annual report itself links the free-float rule to the unused buyback, which is why the two are discussed together.

challenges.challenge: The controller loan is characterised two ways and the valuation takes the harsher one without saying so. Line 128 says the loan's stability and zero interest are 'the behaviour of permanent capital rather than of a demand loan', but the same paragraph says 'a call on that loan would have to be funded', and the bear narrative assumes the loan is called. The bridge deducts the full 41.15bn at face, which is right for a demand loan but too high for permanent capital: a 41.15bn zero-coupon claim discounted at the 7.44% cost of debt over ten years is worth 20.1bn, a 21.05bn (15.4/share, about 12% of the target) difference. The model also charges no interest on the loan in any year, so the 'permanent capital' reading is not consistently applied.
challenges.answer: One characterisation is now applied throughout: the loan is callable. It is deducted at face in the bridge, not discounted, and the bear case carries the cost of a call as a 1pp addition to the cost of capital. The permanent-capital reading is stated and rejected with its value effect: discounting the zero-coupon claim at the 7.44 per cent bank rate over ten years gives about IDR20.1bn, or about IDR15.4 a share more than the face deduction, and we do not take it because the loan has no term and no covenant protecting a minority holder. The loan is unchanged at 30 September 2026, which is the third balance-sheet date on which it has sat still.

challenges.challenge: The report's capital-allocation section omits the share-buyback authorization. S2 states that the company conducted a buyback programme under OJK Regulation 29/2023 and the EGM resolution of 13 June 2025, and that as of 31 December 2025 it had not yet bought any shares. The assumptions say only 'no buyback outstanding', which is true but hides an existing authorization that could be used to support the price, absorb the free float or increase the controller's stake. For a stock at 1.2x book with a 7.81% free float, the authorization is relevant to both the bull (accretion/support) and the governance bear (value transfer to the controller).
challenges.answer: The buyback authorization is now disclosed. It was approved at the 13 June 2025 EGM for up to 10 per cent of paid-up capital and IDR72.22bn, for the period 13 June to 31 December 2025, and no shares had been bought as of 31 December 2025, so the window has closed and a new resolution would be needed to use it. The company itself says the 15 per cent free-float rule constrains a buyback, which is why the authorization is discussed with the dilution rather than as a source of support.

challenges.challenge: Three citations do not support the sentence they attach to. (1) Line 146 says 'the auditor's opinion is unqualified' with [S2, F24], but F24 is the no-legal-cases quote; the archived text contains no auditor's opinion paragraph, so the claim is uncited. (2) Line 66 attributes 'the index consultation on Indonesia's market accessibility' to [S2, F22], but F22 is the shareholder structure and says nothing about an index consultation. (3) Line 44 says the company employed 147 people with [S2, S0, F6], but F6 is installed capacity of 35,000 MT, not headcount. None of these changes the rating, but each is a verifiable citation error.
challenges.answer: Fixed three citation errors: the auditor's opinion sentence is removed because the audit report is not in the archived text; the index-consultation sentence is removed because it was unattributed; and the headcount is now cited to the data pack's own employees field rather than to F6, which is installed capacity.

missing_bull_case.note: F18's 34.68bn 2026 operating-profit target and Q2 2026's 19.8% gross margin are not in the base; the industry's 80-90% remedy utilisation is not in the bull; the buyback authorization is omitted.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear has no down year, no loan-call/refinancing shock despite its narrative, and no free-float dilution; bear gross margin of 17.0% at cost is above the FY2025 11.8% trough.

assumption_realism.note: The 85% pass-through is unsourced and uncalibrated; the 19.5% at-cost gross margin is 2.8pp above the 16.7% ten-year average; base utilisation is 40.7% in FY2027E and 49.0% in FY2030E against an industry at 60-70%.

evidence_and_citations.note: F1-F25 verify and the restatements are right, but the 'does not exceed the FY2022 peak' claim is false, the auditor opinion is uncited, and the index-consultation and headcount citations are misattributed.

valuation_method_fit.note: Trough LTM multiples carry 40% weight and 45% of the DCF-to-blend gap; the P/E leg omits the 41.15bn controller loan; kd is 9.45% against the stated 7.44%; the 7.65% D/E is gross debt over market cap, not net debt to equity.

bias_and_tone.note: The 'price implies peak-cycle' thesis is contradicted by the report's own 25%-probability bull at 294.09 against the 258 price; 'first half 2026 still a fire year' is undercut by Q2 revenue +23.2% y/y and a 19.8% gross margin.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Brent and the macro deck are read consistently, but the commodity-cyclical output contract is missing (through-cycle price and NAV, cost-curve quartile, dividend-capacity yield, net-debt/trough-EBITDA), and the 25% bull is not reconciled to the 42% base rate.

conservatism_audit.note: F18 and the Q2 run-rate are omitted; base utilisation sits below the industry; the controller loan is deducted at face while being called permanent capital; no buyback or free-float dilution is valued.

calibration.note: The 4.80pp EBITDA-margin calibration gap has no qc_justification; the extreme_call's 4.9% ROE matches no model year (FY2025A 1.62%, FY2026E 3.12%, FY2030E 8.26%).

signoff.notes:
APPROVED at sign-off (initiation, round 1, after one red-team return and two QC rounds). Leave at signoff for the Director to publish. Every FATAL/MATERIAL challenge is answered on substance, lint at the draft stage is PASS (one warning, the single-method count, explained in the report), the base is not tilted in either direction by construction, and the batch carries no shared-input tilt: the CHEMICALS industry is mixed (BUY/ADD/HOLD/SELL) and APLI is not the only cautious name.
C1, the FATAL, is properly fixed rather than argued away: the multiple legs are at zero weight, the published target is the DCF, and the report no longer claims a floor exhibit the engine does not compute (Q2). C2 and C10 are rebutted on grounds I accept: the bull is defensible and the price sits between base and bull, and the P/E leg carries zero weight so its missing controller-loan bridge cannot move the target. C3-C9 and C11-C15 are accepted with the arithmetic shown and anchored on the 9M2026 filing (F30-F42) rather than on a first-half extrapolation; I re-checked the FY2026E capex (IDR50.80bn against 9M additions of IDR42.553bn and a cash outlay of IDR46.655bn), the 5.53pp calibration bridge, the loan deduction (IDR41.15bn at face, 1.13x FY2025A EBITDA at 30 Sep 2026) and the 20.2% at-cost gross margin bridge, and they hold.
Batch consistency. APLI is HOLD (target 255, price 258, -0.4%) while CLPI is BUY (2,098): different companies, and the gap is the return, not a shared input. The inputs that could tilt a batch are in line — WACC 11.87% against the industry's 10.5-12.4%, terminal growth 3.0% inside the 2.0-4.0% range, and the 20% illiquidity discount is the same rate CLPI, LTLS, ADMG and SAMF carry, so the HOLD is not manufactured by a discount only APLI receives. APLI is the only 100%-DCF name in the industry, which the role file requires an outlier to justify; the reason is on the record (weights.changed and report section 4) and is the correct application of VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL — the other names' multiple legs sit 30-40% below their DCFs on exactly the trailing-earnings logic C1 rejected, which is a point for the next CHEMICALS refresh, not a defect in this report.
Both directions re-tested. Upward: FY2026E +15.8% is the 9M actual plus a Q4 step-up the restarted calender makes possible, and the 20.2% at-cost margin is bridged from FY2024's 17.2%. Downward: revenue is 33% below the company's own target F17, the bull is 25% against the 42% capex-turnaround base rate, and the target is struck after a 20% liquidity discount. They roughly cancel; the DCF of IDR226 is 12% below the price, which is the honest reading for a HOLD.
Two QC NOTEs carry forward and must be closed in the next revision, neither of which changes the target: N1 — report section 5 and the assumptions bear narrative still say FY2029E and FY2030E revenue fall, but the 8pp shock leaves FY2029E at about +0.5%; only FY2030E falls. N2 — the bear narrative's discounted free-float placement (about 1.5% of value) is not implemented as a shock; either apply it or soften the sentence. N2 is advice only. I am not returning a well-evidenced report to correct one year of prose in a scenario narrative; the Director should note the correction as a publishing condition if the narrative is quoted.
No broker research, rating, target or consensus figure was used or found in the packet; sources are the AR2025, the 30 June and 30 September 2026 interim statements, the dividend notice, industry press and the firm decks. No contamination.

bias.note: Neutral, re-tested both ways. findings.finding: RESOLVED (was FIX). VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL requires NAV per share at the through-cycle price and at spot. The report gives the through-cycle NAV of IDR230 and asserts that holding Brent at spot would raise near-term cash flow without changing terminal value, but publishes no NAV-at-spot figure in the prose or in a table, and the deck spot of IDR97.1 is not shown against the IDR75 long-run price.
findings.answer: We take the second option and state why a spot NAV is not meaningful here, citing the spot source. The deck spot is above the long-run through-cycle price and above every explicit year of the deck path after FY2026E, and the company's exposure is indirect, about a tenth of cost of goods sold after the cost link and pass-through. A DCF with Brent held at spot would therefore capitalise a war premium into perpetuity for a converter that buys resin, which is exactly what the card says spot is not: spot is cycle position, a timing input, never value. The report also withdraws the earlier and wrong claim that holding Brent at spot would raise near-term cash flow: spot is above the deck path, so on our cost link a spot NAV would be lower, not higher, and publishing it would invite the procyclical error in the other direction. The through-cycle NAV of the DCF is stated against the deck's long-run price.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pe': 0.15}
flags.justification: The industry default is a 60/25/15 blend of DCF, EV/EBITDA and P/E, and we have set the two multiple weights to zero so that the target is the DCF. Both multiple legs are struck on trailing LTM figures built from the fire year - the engine capitalises LTM EBITDA of about IDR10bn and LTM net profit of about IDR15bn - which is exactly the procyclical error the commodity-cyclical card forbids, and the engine cannot re-base them on normalised mid-cycle earnings without editing the engine. Removing their weight is therefore the only way to publish a through-cycle target. Because the engine computes only methods that carry a positive weight, no multiple table or floor value exists in this model; we do not claim one, and the cross-checks the report gives are the reverse DCF and the book-value and dividend-capacity anchors, all built from model lines [S0, S2, S4, S5, F5, F7].
